title: Green or White Areas Inside a Tomato: What They Mean

seo.title: Why Is My Tomato Green or White Inside?
seo.meta_description: Firm white or green tissue inside a red tomato often comes from uneven ripening or internal white tissue. Without mold, off odor, or wet decay, it can be used.
seo.search_intent: Explain firm green or white areas inside a red tomato and distinguish ripening disorders from spoilage.

excerpt: Firm white or green areas inside a tomato usually reflect uneven ripening or a physiological disorder rather than rot. If the fruit has no mold, off odor, slime, or wet collapsing tissue, it is generally usable.
content_html:
You cut into a red tomato and find a firm white, pale yellow, or green patch near the core or just under the outer wall. It can look like hidden spoilage, but firm pale tissue is often a ripening or physiological disorder rather than rot.

Tomatoes do not always ripen evenly. High heat, sun exposure, plant nutrition, cultivar, and other growing conditions can leave certain tissues pale and hard even while the rest of the fruit develops normal red color.

Internal white tissue is a recognized tomato disorder

UC Davis lists internal white tissue among physiological disorders that can appear during tomato production and postharvest ripening. The pale tissue may form streaks or firm patches through the fruit wall. University of Minnesota Extension has also reported more internal white tissue after periods of intense heat.

You cannot diagnose the exact growing condition from a sliced tomato at home. What you can do is distinguish firm, dry abnormal tissue from wet, collapsing, decayed tissue.

Green inside a tomato is not the same issue as a green potato

A tomato may retain green internal areas when ripening is uneven. That green color represents chlorophyll and less-mature tissue. It does not invoke the green-potato glycoalkaloid rule.

The main downside is eating quality. Pale or green sections may be firmer, less sweet, and more vegetal-tasting. Trim them if they are unpleasant; a sound tomato does not need to be discarded solely because of that color.

Use texture and moisture to separate quality from spoilage

What the inside looks likeWhat it suggests
Firm white/green patch, dry, normal smellUneven ripening/internal white tissue; trim if desired
Hard pale shoulder near stemPersistent green shoulder or incomplete ripening
Brown/black area that is wet and softDamage or decay; discard if significant
Translucent water-soaked flesh that collapsesSevere injury or rot; discard
Mold or sour/fermented odorDiscard

Can you eat the white part?

Firm white tissue is not known to be hazardous just because of its color. It may be tough or bland, so removing it is often a texture decision rather than a safety requirement.

For sauce, trim out the firm pale core before cooking if you do not want fibrous pieces. If the tomato is already very ripe, use it soon; a physiological defect does not stop normal aging.

Cold storage can create a different set of symptoms

Tomatoes are chilling-sensitive. Too much cold before full ripening can lead to uneven color, poor flavor development, premature softening, pitting, seed browning, and increased decay. That is another reason not to assume every unusual interior has one cause.

The useful rule

Firm white or green tissue usually points to uneven ripening; wet, slimy, foul-smelling, or collapsing tissue points to deterioration. If the pale patch is the only oddity, trim it for quality and use the rest.

faq.question: Why is a red tomato still green inside?
faq.answer: Ripening can be uneven, leaving internal tissue less mature and greener even when the outside has turned red.

faq.question: Can you eat a tomato with white tissue inside?
faq.answer: Usually, yes, when the white area is firm and dry and the tomato has no signs of spoilage. Trim it if the texture is unpleasant.

faq.question: Does white tissue mean the tomato is diseased?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. Internal white tissue is a recognized physiological disorder associated with growing conditions such as heat.
